text:
## Abstract

This query compared two Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) accession identifiers, GSE309890 (a Series) and GDS309890 (a purported DataSet), to determine whether they refer to the same underlying record. The GEO database was queried directly via the `geo_series` tool, which accepts any GEO accession type (GSE, GPL, GSM, GDS) and resolves it to its corresponding Entrez `gds` UID and metadata. GSE309890 resolved to a fully populated record: an *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655 RNA-seq Series titled "Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway," with 6 samples, platform GPL24659, BioProject PRJNA1363958, and one supplementary FPKM file. GDS309890, in contrast, resolved to an empty record: no title, summary, taxon, experiment type, platform, or samples were returned, and no supplementary files exist at the corresponding GDS FTP path. This demonstrates that "GSE309890" and "GDS309890" are not the same object and, on current evidence, GDS309890 does not exist as a valid, populated GEO DataSet. The distinction matters because GSE and GDS accession numbers are independent numbering series in GEO — a shared numeral does not imply record identity or even inter-conversion via UID arithmetic in the way it does within a single accession type.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) hosts several related but structurally distinct record types: Series (GSE), Samples (GSM), Platforms (GPL), and curated DataSets (GDS). GDS records are a legacy, thinly populated, curator-assembled layer built on top of Series/Sample data; not every Series has a corresponding GDS. Accession prefixes distinguish record types, but the numeric suffix is assigned independently for each prefix, so "GSE309890" and "GDS309890" sharing the digits "309890" carries no guarantee of any relationship.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. The `geo_series` call for GSE309890 reported `pubmed_ids: []` with the note that no PubMed record is linked to this GEO record.

**Knowledge Gap.** It was not established, prior to querying, whether GDS309890 was (a) an alternate accession for the same study as GSE309890, (b) a distinct curated DataSet derived from different data, or (c) a non-existent/unassigned accession.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to determine, using direct GEO metadata retrieval, whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 designate the same record. The tested expectation was that shared numeric suffixes across different GEO prefixes do not imply record identity, and that GDS309890 would either be unrelated to or absent relative to GSE309890.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** Both accessions were queried independently and identically using the same tool, allowing a direct side-by-side comparison of returned metadata fields.

**Materials.** NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), queried via the `geo_series` tool (which wraps NCBI E-utilities `esummary` against the `gds` Entrez database).

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)` — default file listing enabled.
2. `geo_series(accession="GDS309890", list_files=true)` — default file listing enabled.

Each call resolves the accession to a `gds` Entrez UID, fetches its `esummary` record, and additionally attempts to list the corresponding FTP supplementary-files directory.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistical computation was performed. All values reported (sample count = 6, supplementary file count = 1 vs. 0) are read directly from the tool's structured output fields (`sample_count`, `supplementary_files`), with no deduplication or derived percentages needed.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

Table 1. Comparison of GSE309890 and GDS309890 metadata retrieved from GEO.

| Field | GSE309890 | GDS309890 |
|---|---|---|
| Resolved UID | 200309890 | 309890 |
| Entry type | GSE (Series) | (empty — no record populated) |
| Title | "Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback" | (empty) |
| Taxon | *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | (empty) |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | (empty) |
| Platform | GPL24659 | (empty) |
| Sample count | 6 | (empty) |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 | (empty) |
| PubMed links | none | none |
| Supplementary files | 1 (GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz, 510K) | 0 (directory does not exist) |
| GEO URL | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890 | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890 |

**Findings.** GSE309890 returned a fully populated Series record with 6 samples and 1 supplementary file. GDS309890 returned no title, taxon, experiment type, platform, sample list, or BioProject, and its expected supplementary directory (`https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/soft/`) does not exist per the tool's note. The two accessions resolved to different Entrez UIDs (200309890 vs. 309890), confirming they are handled as distinct records within GEO's internal indexing, and only one of the two (GSE309890) carries retrievable content.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not the same record. GSE309890 is a real, populated Series describing an RNA-seq experiment on sertraline-driven antibiotic resistance in *E. coli*. GDS309890 returned no data of any kind, consistent with either (a) no such DataSet having been assigned/curated at that accession, or (b) the digits "309890" coincidentally overlapping between the two unrelated numbering series.

**Context.** No related literature (PubMed) is linked to GSE309890, so no external record corroborates or names a companion GDS accession for this study. This is consistent with the study's apparent unpublished/pre-indexing status.

**Limitations.** The tool's own provenance note states that GEO's API returns metadata only, not processed expression values, and that for GDS records the accession-to-UID mapping rule differs from other GEO types — meaning an incorrect mapping could, in principle, return "a real record of another type rather than an error." The empty result for GDS309890 was checked against this risk and found to genuinely reflect an unpopulated/absent record rather than a misrouted one, but absence of a curator-built GDS does not itself prove no GDS will ever be built from this Series' data.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 and GDS309890 are distinct identifiers, and GDS309890 does not presently resolve to any populated GEO content. Anyone citing "GDS309890" as equivalent to GSE309890 would be in error based on current GEO records. A useful follow-up query would be `geo_search(term="sertraline", organism="Escherichia coli", entry_type="gds")` to confirm whether any curated DataSet exists at all for this study under a different accession.

## References
[1] NCBI GEO, GSE309890 — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO, supplementary file directory for GSE309890 — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[3] NCBI GEO, GDS309890 (queried, no populated record) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890
[4] NCBI GEO, expected supplementary directory for GDS309890 (does not exist) — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/soft/
[5] NCBI Entrez E-utilities esummary API call for GSE309890 — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi (db=gds, id=200309890)
[6] NCBI Entrez E-utilities esummary API call for GDS309890 — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi (db=gds, id=309890)

## Acknowledgments
This analysis used metadata provided by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database.
